neighbours.label: the speaker framing their own statement: ' I' in all I can say / I think / I tell you, ' you' in as you can see
fire: After a week with the new phone, all I can say is that the battery is excellent.
The match was close, but honestly, I think we deserved the win tonight.
Working on the night shift is exhausting, I tell you, and nobody thanks you.
As you can see from the chart, sales doubled in the second quarter.
The soup was, I must say, the best thing on the whole menu.
Well, I guess the trip went better than any of us expected.
Moving house is stressful, I can tell you that from experience.
The ending was, I suppose, a little too neat for my taste.
quiet: After a week with the new phone, I charged it only twice in total.
The match was close, and I scored the second goal tonight.
Working on the night shift, I drove home at six every morning.
From the chart, sales doubled in the second quarter of the year.
The soup I ordered was the best thing on the whole menu.
On the trip I visited three cities and two small villages.
When moving house, I packed every box myself over two weekends.
At the ending I closed the book and went to sleep.

notes: card: ' I' x7 in 'All I can say', 'Very well, I think', 'nerve-racking, I tell you'; logit promotes can/if/will. Near misses use ' I' as an ordinary narrative subject.
